name: Amazon Timestream
tagline: AWS time-series services: managed InfluxDB today, with serverless LiveAnalytics closed to new customers.
description: Amazon Timestream launched in 2020 as a serverless, SQL-queried time-series database with automatic tiering from memory to magnetic storage, now branded Timestream for LiveAnalytics. In 2024 AWS added Timestream for InfluxDB, a managed InfluxDB service that now offers InfluxDB 2 instances and InfluxDB 3 Enterprise clusters. On June 20, 2025 AWS closed LiveAnalytics to new customers and began steering them to the InfluxDB option; existing LiveAnalytics workloads keep running and still get security and availability work. For a new AWS project, think of Timestream as managed InfluxDB and compare it with running InfluxDB, Tiger Cloud or Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus.
statusNote: Timestream for LiveAnalytics closed to new customers on 2025-06-20 (existing workloads unaffected); AWS points new users to Timestream for InfluxDB.

license.name: Proprietary AWS service (InfluxDB engine is open source)

pricing.notes: Timestream for InfluxDB bills instance-hours and storage; LiveAnalytics bills writes, storage and query compute units.

scale.notes: LiveAnalytics scales automatically; InfluxDB 3 Enterprise clusters scale by adding nodes, InfluxDB 2 instances scale up.

strengths: Fully managed on AWS with IAM, KMS encryption and VPC integration
Timestream for InfluxDB keeps standard InfluxDB APIs, so Telegraf and Grafana work unchanged
LiveAnalytics needs no capacity planning for existing users
Choice of InfluxDB 2 (Flux) or InfluxDB 3 Enterprise clusters
weaknesses: LiveAnalytics, the original serverless engine, is closed to new customers
AWS-only; Timestream for InfluxDB is mostly a hosted open-source engine with AWS pricing
Instance-based InfluxDB pricing is less elastic than the original serverless model
Migrating off LiveAnalytics requires a data export and query rewrite
useCases: IoT telemetry on AWS IoT Core
notIdealFor: New projects expecting the LiveAnalytics serverless model
